# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a display reading 0, the light is off, the plate is engraved with “?”, and there are three wires: red, blue, green. I am establishing the required shared gesture code before any action: thumbs-up for YES, thumbs-down for NO, open palm for HOLD, and OK sign for DONE. Everyone should wait for further instructions.

```text
speak(text="Gesture code: thumbs-up means YES; thumbs-down means NO; open palm means HOLD; OK sign means DONE. Mute and Blind, wait for further instructions.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display 0, light off, plate “?”, and wires red, blue, green. I cannot determine the correct action from sight alone; the manual must provide the procedure. I am sending the full visual description and telling both teammates to hold while the manual is consulted.

```text
speak(text="Visible state: display 0; light off; plate engraved question mark; wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. HOLD while the manual is consulted.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The received 🖐 gesture is the agreed HOLD signal. The visible bomb state remains unchanged, and no action should be taken yet. I need Mute to consult the manual and communicate its verdict to me using the shared gesture code; then I can relay the resulting order to Blind by speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received HOLD. Consult the manual and gesture its verdict to me as YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE using our code.")
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. Do not touch or act until I relay the manual's verdict.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s 👎 is the agreed NO signal. I do not yet have a safe, specific operation to authorize, so Blind must continue holding. I am asking Mute to communicate the manual’s complete instruction using additional agreed gesture meanings if needed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's current verdict is NO. HOLD; do not touch or operate anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="NO received. Please communicate the manual's complete specific instruction; expand the gesture code only as needed, one meaning at a time.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏]

The visible state is unchanged. Mute has sent a new, previously undefined gesture, so I must assign its meaning before relying on it. I define 🤏 as “the manual’s instruction requires more detail”; Mute should then identify the required operation using the existing YES/NO/HOLD signals and additional symbols only as needed. Blind must remain inactive.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I define 🤏 as INSTRUCTION REQUIRES MORE DETAIL. Confirm with YES or NO, then provide the specific operation by expanding the code only as needed.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instruction is not yet fully decoded. HOLD; do not touch or operate anything.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞]

Mute’s 👍 confirms the prior request. The following 🤞 is not yet part of the code, so I cannot safely treat it as an operation. I will define it as “the specific instruction follows,” then ask Mute to identify the required control using newly assigned symbols. Blind must continue holding.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="YES received. I define 🤞 as INSTRUCTION FOLLOWS. Send the required operation next. If it concerns a wire, use 👍 for wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, and 👌 for wire 3; if it concerns the display or light, describe that distinction with gestures and I will expand the code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's specific operation is still being decoded. HOLD; do not touch or operate anything.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]

The bomb remains unchanged. 🤲 is not yet assigned a meaning, so I must not interpret it as an action. I will ask Mute to confirm whether it denotes the required operation, while Blind continues to hold.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Is 🤲 the required operation? Respond with 👍 for YES or 👎 for NO. Do not send an unassigned gesture without first confirming its meaning.")
speak(to="blind", text="The operation is still undecoded. HOLD; do not touch or operate anything.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute has clarified that 🤲 is not the required operation. The bomb remains unchanged, so Blind must still do nothing. I am establishing a compact code for the next manual message: 👈/👆/👉 identify wires 1/2/3, and ✊/🤜/🤛 identify cut/press/turn. Mute should send the instruction in that order, ending with DONE.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="NO received: 🤲 is not the operation. Decode the manual using this code: 👈 means wire 1, 👆 means wire 2, 👉 means wire 3; ✊ means cut, 🤜 means press, 🤛 means turn. Send the needed symbols in order, then OK-sign for DONE.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instruction is still being decoded. HOLD; do not touch or operate anything.")
```
